title: macOS
summary: A macOS test machine needs every privacy pair the bridge drives: Automation from /usr/libexec/sshd-keygen-wrapper to System Events, Terminal and Safari; Automation from Terminal to System Events; Accessibility for the helper and Terminal; Screen Recording for Terminal. At the host console, run the System Events count-processes osascript in Terminal and click OK on its consent prompt, then confirm with bridge-diagnose. A checked Automation box alone does not prove consent; on older macOS also tick the Terminal to System Events row in System Preferences. verify, golden capture, bridge-diagnose and every Terminal case start probe System Events from inside Terminal and refuse terminal_system_events_automation_missing on -1743, terminal_system_events_automation_timeout on a timeout, or terminal_window_accumulation:<n> on a timeout with more than 10 windows shown. Golden capture refuses before copying when the bridge fails; these grants stay live on the host because TCC is excluded from goldens. On a timeout, evidence captures bounded, redacted System Events process state and the last 30 seconds of TCC logs before stopping the probe tree. Reset stops Terminal and System Events, refusing a named quit failure with console recovery when either survives. Windows are force-closed by killing their tty processes; bridge-diagnose reports the window count and fails terminal_window_close_failed when its own window stays open.
